title: The Arctic and the Antarctic
summary: How Earth's two cold polar regions compare: the Arctic is a frozen ocean ringed by land, the Antarctic is an icy continent that is also a desert, and each has its own animals and people.
poll: I would rather visit the Antarctic than the Arctic.

versions.title: Two Cold Ends
versions.text:
Our world has two cold ends. One is at the top. It is the Arctic. One is at the bottom. It is the Antarctic. Each has a pole.

Why are they so cold? The sun is low in the sky there. Its light is weak. In the hot months, the sun does not set. In the cold months, it is dark all day.

The north end is a sea. The sea is frozen. Ice floats on top. Land is all around it.

The south end is land. It is a big continent. Thick ice sits on it. It is the coldest place of all.

It is a desert, too! A desert gets very little rain or snow. This one is cold, not hot.

Polar bears live in the north. They hunt seals on the ice. Penguins live in the south. So bears and penguins do not meet!

People have lived in the north for a long time. No one lives in the south all year. Teams come to study it.

Now the ice melts. The world is warm. Teams check the ice.

versions.title: Two Cold Ends
versions.text:
Our world has two very cold ends. The one at the top is the Arctic. The one at the bottom is the Antarctic. Each one has a pole.

Why are they so cold? At the poles, the sun stays low in the sky. Its light is weak. In summer, the sun does not set at all. In winter, it stays dark for weeks.

The north end is mostly sea. The sea is frozen, and ice floats on top. Land is all around it.

The south end is land. It is a huge continent. Thick ice sits on top of it. It is the coldest place in the world.

It is a desert, too! A desert gets very little rain or snow. This desert is cold, not hot.

Polar bears live in the north. They hunt seals on the ice. Penguins live in the far south. So bears and penguins never meet in the wild!

People have lived in the north for thousands of years. No one lives in the south all year. Just a few teams of scientists go there to study it.

Now the ice is melting as the world gets warm. Scientists check the ice to learn more.

Now the ice is melting as Earth gets warm. Scientists study the ice to learn more.

versions.title: The Arctic and the Antarctic
versions.text:
Earth has two very cold ends. The region at the top is called the Arctic, and the region at the bottom is called the Antarctic. The North Pole is in the Arctic, and the South Pole is in the Antarctic.

Why are these places so cold? Near the poles, the sun stays low in the sky, so its light is weak and spread out. In summer, the sun does not set at all. In winter, it can stay dark for weeks.

The Arctic is mostly an ocean. Much of this ocean is frozen, so a layer of ice floats on top. Land surrounds it on many sides.

The Antarctic is very different. It is a huge continent made of land, and thick ice covers almost all of it. It is the coldest place on Earth.

Surprisingly, the Antarctic is also a desert. A desert is a place that gets very little rain or snow. This desert is freezing, not hot like the deserts of Saudi Arabia.

Polar bears live in the Arctic, where they hunt seals on the ice. Penguins live in the far south. That means polar bears and penguins never meet in the wild!

People have lived in the Arctic for thousands of years. But no one lives in the Antarctic all year. Only scientists visit to study it.

Today, the ice is melting as Earth gets warmer. Scientists study the ice to learn how our planet is changing.

versions.title: The Arctic and the Antarctic
versions.text:
Earth has two very cold ends, called the polar regions. The region at the top of the globe is the Arctic, and the region at the bottom is the Antarctic. The North Pole lies in the Arctic, and the South Pole lies in the Antarctic.

Both regions are cold because sunlight reaches them at a low angle. The light spreads over a wide area, so it gives less heat. In summer, the sun never sets. In winter, it can stay dark for weeks.

Although they are both cold, the two regions are built very differently. The Arctic is mostly an ocean. Much of it is frozen, so a floating layer of ice covers the water. Land surrounds it on many sides.

The Antarctic is a continent, a huge area of land. A thick ice sheet covers almost all of it. It is the coldest place on Earth.

The Antarctic is also a desert, because it gets very little rain or snow. It is a frozen desert, quite unlike the hot deserts of Saudi Arabia.

Polar bears live in the Arctic and hunt seals on the ice. Penguins live in the far south, so the two animals never meet in the wild.

People have lived in the Arctic for thousands of years. No one lives in the Antarctic all year. Instead, scientists visit research stations to study it.

Today, the polar ice is shrinking as Earth grows warmer, and scientists measure it closely.

The Antarctic is also a desert, because it receives very little rain or snow each year. It is a frozen desert, quite unlike the hot, sandy deserts of Saudi Arabia.

Polar bears live in the Arctic and hunt seals on the floating ice. Penguins live in the far south, so these two animals never meet in the wild.

People have lived in the Arctic for thousands of years, fishing and hunting along its icy coasts. Nobody lives in the Antarctic permanently; instead, scientists visit research stations to study it.

Today, the polar ice is shrinking as Earth grows warmer, and scientists measure these changes carefully because they affect the entire planet.

versions.title: The Arctic and the Antarctic: Opposite Ends of Earth
versions.text:
Earth has two extremely cold ends, known as the polar regions. The region surrounding the top of the globe is the Arctic, located in the Northern Hemisphere, while the region at the bottom is the Antarctic, located in the Southern Hemisphere. The North Pole lies in the Arctic, and the South Pole lies in the Antarctic.

Both regions are cold because sunlight reaches them at a low angle. This spreads its energy across a wide area and delivers considerably less heat than it does near the equator. In summer, the sun never sets, but in winter, it can remain below the horizon for weeks at a time.

Although both regions are frigid, their geography is very different. The Arctic is mostly an ocean, much of which is frozen, so a floating layer of sea ice covers the water. Land belonging to several countries, including Canada, Russia, and Norway, surrounds it.

The Antarctic, by contrast, is a continent, an enormous landmass buried beneath an ice sheet that is more than four kilometers thick in places. It is the coldest location on Earth, where scientists once recorded a temperature of approximately minus 89 degrees Celsius.

Remarkably, the Antarctic is also a desert, because it receives very little precipitation, meaning rain or snow, each year. It is a frozen desert, entirely unlike the scorching, sandy deserts of Saudi Arabia. Yet its ice sheet holds most of the fresh water on the planet.

Because the two hemispheres experience opposite seasons, the Antarctic summer occurs during December and January, when the Arctic is dark.

Polar bears inhabit the Arctic and hunt seals on the drifting ice, whereas penguins live in the far south, so the two never encounter each other in the wild.

Indigenous peoples have lived in the Arctic for thousands of years, fishing and hunting along its icy coastlines. Nobody lives in the Antarctic permanently; instead, scientists work at research stations, and an international treaty protects the continent for peaceful science.

Today, the polar ice is shrinking as Earth grows warmer, and scientists monitor these changes carefully, because melting ice can raise sea levels and affect communities everywhere.

versions.title: The Arctic and the Antarctic: Opposite Ends of Earth
versions.text:
Earth has two extremely cold extremities, known as the polar regions. The region surrounding the top of the globe is the Arctic, located in the Northern Hemisphere, while the region at the bottom is the Antarctic, located in the Southern Hemisphere; the North Pole lies in the Arctic, and the South Pole lies in the Antarctic.

Both regions are cold because sunlight reaches them at a low angle, which distributes its energy across an extensive area and delivers considerably less heat than it does near the equator. In summer, the sun never sets, but in winter, it can remain below the horizon for weeks at a time.

Indigenous peoples have inhabited the Arctic for thousands of years, fishing and hunting along its icy coastlines. Nobody lives in the Antarctic permanently; instead, scientists work at research stations, and an international treaty protects the continent for peaceful scientific investigation.
